chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) at the funeral of a man from our companions. So when they buried him, he (peace be upon him) stood at his grave and threw soil upon it from the side facing his head three times with his handful. Then he spread his palm upon the grave and said: 'O Allah! Widen the earth for him on his two sides, and ascend his soul to You, and grant him pleasure from You, and settle in his grave from Your mercy that which makes him independent of the mercy of anyone other than You.' Then he went away.

key_terms.جَافِ الْأَرْضَ: Widen/expand the earth (referring to the grave)
key_terms.حَثَى: To throw or scatter soil with the hand

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for spreading soil on a grave and the associated supplication according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrated the recommended etiquette of spreading soil specifically from the head side, a practice emphasized by Shia jurists as a sunnah of the Prophet and Imams. The accompanying supplication invokes divine mercy to ensure the deceased's self-sufficiency in Allah's grace, reflecting the Shia theological emphasis on intercession and the spiritual state of the soul immediately after burial.
